title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s White Day Part 6
text: The mutant races forward at a speed that seems to say it has awakened.
“W-what is that? That Filolial?”
“I’m pretty sure it said ‘hybrid’ on the sign.”
“It’s no use trying to catch up. How far do you think it is behind the leading pack?”
Although voices like these can be heard, the spectators cannot ignore the glow in the distance. And then, the mutant begins to advance.

Spectators watching from afar hold their breath… After all, even though their eyes had grown accustomed to the speed of the Filolial King and Queen—whom they’d always considered fast—the mutant Filolial’s speed is so overwhelming that the leading pack appears slow by comparison. With every step it takes, the mutant closes in on the leading pack at a terrifying pace… leaving afterimages in its wake. In fact, it’s running just like the blue afterimage from that famous fighting game.

Eventually, one by one, it overtook them until it had completely caught up to the leading pack. The Thoroughbred glanced back once and seemed to smile. It understood what was coming… sensing a connection as if its Rival had finally caught up. What kind of twist is this? Is this a racing story?

“”

As if using up every last bit of stamina, the Thoroughbred unleashes Filo’s special move, Spiral Strike, and flies toward the finish line. …Meanwhile, the Mutant seemed to be transforming its tail feathers into multiple tails, rapidly gathering Magical Power to cast High Quick. And then… it created clones, using the multiplied versions of itself to push forward.
“Haaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa!?”
“Whaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaat!?”
Yeah. I did warn the Filolial Race organizers that there might be a problem with this running style. But they kept insisting there was no issue. I warned them. I won’t accept any complaints.

Sure enough, cries of astonishment rang out from the crowd. The variant Filolial used the clones it had just created as a springboard to accelerate even further, unleashing both Spiral Strike and High Quick. The mutant crossed the finish line about half a horse length ahead of the Thoroughbred at a speed too fast for the eye to follow.
The sheer velocity sent a shockwave rippling through the racecourse, triggering a tornado. The Filolials who had retired and were resting used Magic to calm it down.
“Kue… Kue…”
“Kue!”
The Thoroughbred, gasping for breath, sat down while the Filolial struck a victory pose.
“W-what is this!? Is this even allowed?”
“Wait a minute! Sure, the race rules and that Filolial’s pedigree were clearly listed… but what’s going on here!?”
A heated debate erupted among the spectators. I guess that’s to be expected.

That’s right… I think some of you might have had a hunch based on its coloration… but that thing is a hybrid between a Filolial and a Raph-species. It hatched from a Filolial egg laid by one of the Filolials that Chick had been scolding. Rat and Taniko were curious to see how it would turn out, and at the recommendation of the race organizers, I raised it—that’s that guy.

This Filolial possesses abilities that combine the characteristics of both the Queen and the Raph-species. It’s the concept of the “Hengen Muso Style”—absorbing Magical Power and Ki from the air… which is what Filo was doing before she was taught the technique—and with this power, it replenishes its Magical Power incredibly quickly. It’s also fast on its feet and skilled at using Magic.

Its elemental type is an illusion and wind hybrid, like a mix of Raphtalia and Filo… but in terms of category, it leans toward the support type. She’s not good at offensive wind magic, but she excels at creating clones and deceiving her opponents’ eyes. The Magic she used this time was her own unique technique—creating a physical clone and sharing her stamina with it… If breathing becomes difficult, the clone breathes for her; if she runs out of Magical Power, the clone… it takes over everything for her.

When she focuses her mind on running, she’s incredible. Although the effect lasts only a short time, the fact remains that it was enough to win this extreme race… That’s the result we’re left with. In addition to its Filolial form, it can take on a large Raph-species form. However, the downside is that it has a rather niche set of abilities—it cannot take human form or speak human language.
“Wait a minute—we were given the details beforehand. This race was always meant to turn conventional wisdom on its head. I won’t complain.”
“But is that really okay?”
“It’s fine, right? We’re allowed to use Magic for anything other than attacking. Even in a normal Filolial race, the Filolials cast support spells on themselves, don’t they!”

A heated debate began among the spectators. Meanwhile, race officials came out to present awards to the Filolials. This race is shaping up to be a total mess. This is the first edition, but… the results are likely to be controversial.
“Gwaaaaaaaah!”

‘I did it!’ the mutant says, flapping its wings at me. Its tail’s turned into a Raph-species one. Actually, the pattern on its belly is a Raph-species one too. When it’s lying on its back, it looks just like that yokai that lives next door. …Filo pulled that stunt a few times, too. Well, Raph-species generally look like that when they grow larger.
It takes the trophy with a bit of a skip in its step and waves its hand.
“Guaaaaaa…”
Oh, it closed its eyes. Looks like the excitement has worn off. It closes them when its motivation drops, doesn’t it? It looks sleepy.
“Guaaaaa…”

The Thoroughbred approaches the mutant, claps, and holds out a wing to shake hands. I don’t quite understand the words, but it seems to be praising it. Then, the moment it gets right in front of the mutant’s face.
Chomp!
The mutant bit down on the Thoroughbred’s head, taking it whole.
“Guaaaaaaaaaaa!”
The Filolials around them rush over, grabbing the mutant and the Thoroughbred to try to pull them apart.
“Waaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!?”
“W-what’s going on!?”

Well, its mouth is huge… or rather, why did it even bite down in the first place? The Thoroughbred was thrashing about, but the bite was so tight it must have been suffocating him—he gradually started convulsing. As it was, the mutant slowly lifted the Thoroughbred up and started crunching… There’s no way that’s going to fit… Wait, no—they’re monsters. Maybe my common sense doesn’t apply here.
“Kue! Kue!”
“Master! Activate the Monster Crest!”

Midori and the other Tri-Color Filolials rushed over to me. Ah, right—Motoyasu isn’t here. Apparently, the Philos are still having a fan meeting over there. I think they mentioned something about making a joint photo book or something. I hurriedly activated the mutant’s monster mark to trigger the penalty. I finally managed to rescue the Thoroughbred from the mutant.
“Why would you do something like this…?”
As I stroked and calmed the Variant—which was staring intently at the Thoroughbred, waiting for an opening—Midori and the others listened to the explanation from the other Filolials.
“Um… apparently, they made a rule that whoever wins this match gets to give an order, and the loser has to obey it.”
Midori pointed at the Thoroughbred, who was rolling its eyes, as she answered.
“Huh… So why did this guy try to eat him?”
“Why?”
“Kuuuuuuh!”
“Ah, yes. One more time, yes… yes.”
Midori asked several times before the creature nodded. Later, I heard from Filo that the creature’s speech was hard to understand because it was a hybrid.
“‘Since I won, it’s dinner!’ That’s what it said.”
“Cannibalism, though…”
“Master, based on this one’s perception, it’s doubtful whether it even sees us as its own kind.”

Hmm… It looks like a Filolial, but is its inner nature different? What a strange creature. The Thoroughbred is staring intently at the mutant. It must be terrifying to nearly get eaten by someone you thought was your Rival.
“Anyway, you mustn’t eat anyone from the village or the surrounding areas.”
So this is what Imiya meant when she said she felt a chill. Filo had stepped on this landmine once before, but this one is far more of a glutton than Filo.
“Guh!”

It’s saluting as if to say “Got it,” but I’m not buying it. If they weren’t from the village or the surrounding area, it’d probably eat them. It seems like the kind of creature that would exploit that loophole.

Just as we were talking about that, Filo appeared, landing with a thud after spinning several times high in the sky. I don’t get it. Is this a downside of being an idol? I actually found it kind of cool for a second there.
“Filo to the rescue! Master, you were over here!”
“Well, yeah…”

The venue is still buzzing with excitement. The payouts have started, but… the results left some people dissatisfied. Since even the experts had a hard time predicting this race, it turned into a massive long shot. I’d placed bets on all the Filolials, just in case. Well, thanks to betting a bit more on the variants because I’d raised them with such affection, I actually made a decent profit.
“At a rate like this, the crowd won’t be satisfied, so how about an exhibition race with Filo, you guys, and—while we’re at it—this glutton?”
“What about Mokkun?”
“No idea. Go get him if you want. If you tell him Filo’s running, he’ll come running.”
“‘Booh!’”
Saying things like that, the three-colored Filolials went to fetch Motoyasu, and the exhibition race began.
“Master! Is it okay for Filo to run?”
Filo asked excitedly, her eyes sparkling.
“Yeah, go ahead and run to your heart’s content. But you were singing and dancing just a moment ago. Aren’t you tired?”
“I’m fine! Filo will do her best!”
“Yeah, I’m rooting for you. And… don’t fly. Run on the same ground as the Three-Color Gang.”
“Okay!”
And so, Filo and the others’ race started pretty quickly. The result? Of course Filo won, right?
No twists, no excitement. Ignoring even the Variant’s top speed, Filo just raced off at high speed. Not fun at all. Seriously, it wasn’t fun at all.

We really have the Claw Hero to thank for that. Actually, the Mutant came in last out of the whole group. Just how big is the gap between them? As a result, Filo and the Three-Colored Ones ended up in the “ineligible to compete” category—that’s the punchline. Well, maybe because of that, the King & Queen Cup was well-received by the audience—a double punchline. Yeah, that’s right. Next time we enter Philo and the others, maybe we’ll invite Fitoria too.
